topic.subject: social
topic.title: Motions of the Earth
topic.scope: rotation, revolution, axis tilt, seasons, solstices and equinoxes, leap year

misconceptions.statement: The sun moves across the sky while the Earth stays still.
misconceptions.why: This is based on the direct sensory experience of watching the sun rise and set every day.
misconceptions.fix: The Earth spins on its axis from west to east, which makes the sun appear to move across the sky.

probe.question: Why does the sun rise in the east and set in the west?
probe.wrong_answer: Because the sun travels around the Earth every day.

misconceptions.statement: The Earth is tilted because it is leaning to one side like a falling object.
misconceptions.why: Students often interpret diagrams of the tilted axis as a physical object that is unstable or falling.
misconceptions.fix: The Earth's axis is an imaginary line that is tilted at an angle of 23.5 degrees relative to its orbital plane, and it stays in this fixed orientation.

probe.question: What would happen if the Earth stopped tilting?
probe.wrong_answer: It would fall over and crash into space.

misconceptions.statement: Summer happens because the Earth gets closer to the sun during its orbit.
misconceptions.why: Students often assume that proximity to a heat source is the only reason for temperature changes.
misconceptions.fix: Seasons are caused by the tilt of the Earth's axis as it revolves around the sun, which changes how directly sunlight hits different parts of the Earth.

probe.question: Why is it hotter in summer than in winter?
probe.wrong_answer: Because the Earth is physically closer to the sun in the summer.

misconceptions.statement: The entire Earth experiences the same season at the same time.
misconceptions.why: Students generalize their local experience of weather to the entire planet.
misconceptions.fix: When the Northern Hemisphere is tilted towards the sun and experiences summer, the Southern Hemisphere is tilted away and experiences winter.

probe.question: If it is winter in India, what season is it in Australia?
probe.wrong_answer: It is also winter because the whole Earth is cold.

misconceptions.statement: An equinox means the sun is directly above the equator for the whole day.
misconceptions.why: Students misinterpret the term 'equal night' as a static state rather than a specific moment in the orbit.
misconceptions.fix: An equinox is the specific time when the sun's rays fall vertically on the equator, resulting in equal day and night across the entire globe.

probe.question: What happens during an equinox?
probe.wrong_answer: The sun stays fixed over the equator all day long.
